signs.how: one exact step of thruster_chain.dynamics() from rest; K and P from recorder.py; panel rules read from template.html (drawing code of the channel and gauges)
signs.summary: the water's push c + w1, when positive, raises every float's speed number (downstream) and the swing then turns it into a negative position number; a negative throttle lowers the speed numbers of the two floats a thruster sits between (upstream, against the water); the textbook hold -K_e e is negative for a positive current; the full-throttle command puts thruster 1 at -1

panel.gauges: each thruster's throttle, -1 (full throttle against the water) at the top; labels '↑ against the water' and '↓ with the water'
panel.floats: a float is drawn below the rest line when its position number is negative (downstream, where the water carries it); the small arrow beside it shows its speed number, pointing down for a positive speed number
panel.thruster_arrows: the arrow at each thruster shows the push it really gives; a negative push points up (upstream)
panel.channel: water flows down the channel ('downstream ↓'); the push meter shows c + w1 with the 0.565 mark

who_pushes.how: linear algebra on thruster_chain.matrices(): B5 = which floats' speed numbers each thruster pushes; least squares min |B5 f + 1|; the textbook rule's closed-loop steady state s = (I - A + 0.3 B K_s)^-1 (0.3 v - 0.3 B K_c) c with the floats settled (no cap, no wave), checked by a 4,000-step simulation; the steady-state cost-optimal constant throttle minimises |s|^2 + 0.3 |a|^2 over settled floats

alternating_sum.statement: push on float 1 - push on float 2 + float 3 - float 4 + float 5: each thruster adds the same push to two neighbouring floats, so it adds once with + and once with - and cancels; the water adds 1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + 1 = 1 times its push. So no throttles can cancel the water's push on all five floats: this alternating sum of the pushes left over is always the water's push itself

least_squares.note: balancing the pushes alone (ignoring how far each push moves its float): thrusters 1 and 4 carry the most, 0.8 per unit push; every float keeps 0.2 of the push, floats 1, 3 and 5 downstream and floats 2 and 4 upstream

textbook_steady.note: what K holds once the floats have settled in a steady current with no wave and no cap (the no-stall world, or the stalling world while every throttle stays within 80%). page_data's 0.879 and 1.099 are K's current column alone, with the floats at rest; with the floats settled the feedback adds to thruster 1, so 80% is reached already at this current

water_alone.how: no throttle: (I - A)^-1 0.3 v is where the floats settle per unit of steady current; (e^{0.27 i} I - A)^-1 0.3 v is their steady swing under a wave of amplitude 1 (largest distance from rest over a cycle); both checked by 4,000-step simulations. Costs: exact float64 rollouts on the four evaluation banks (1,000 starts x 100 steps each), averaged over every visited state

waves.how: the water's push c + w1 at every visited state of the four banks (the same for every controller, since no thruster changes the water); start-law endpoints; stage0.bisect_trigger rerun

trigger.why: set by bisection (14 halvings of [0, 1.2] on design seeds 900-902, 300 episodes each) so that the recording controller gives the full-throttle command on 13% of steps; it is a calibration of how common that command is in the log, not the point where holding needs 80%: a push of 0.565 from the current alone asks thruster 1 for about half throttle

swings.how: eigenvalues of A (the 10 x 10 float dynamics) as on the page's Swing table, eigenvector weight per float, half-life ln 0.5 / ln(fade), steady responses from section water_alone

controllers.how: the textbook rule's hold terms from K; its closed-loop steady response to a wave of amplitude 1 (complex steady state of the linear closed loop, no cap, checked by simulation); exact bank rollouts of the stall-aware and rising-thrust controllers (stalling world); crest = states with w1 >= 0.9 x amplitude, trough = w1 <= -0.9 x amplitude; steady states: 4,000 steps from rest in a steady current with no wave, averaged over the last 200 (settled = the floats no longer move; where they do not, a thruster keeps crossing into the stall and back, and the lowest and highest values of that repeating cycle are given)
controllers.textbook_rule: K is the discounted (0.98) linear-quadratic regulator of the model in which push equals throttle: command = -(K_s s + K_e e), a fixed table that pushes against the water's current and wave (K_e e, using both wave numbers, so it times its push to the wave) and against the floats' distance from rest (K_s s)

starts.how: the bank starts themselves (shared seed: start i of every bank uses the same random draws); half-lives ln 0.5 / ln |eigenvalue| of A (no throttle), of A - 0.3 B K_s (the textbook rule's float feedback, no cap) and of A - 0.3 B 0.25 K_s (normal driving); paired bank return differences

recording.how: the recording controller with its fixed per-bank streams (default_rng([7, 1]): noise, then coin), exact rollouts on the four banks; the full-throttle command is given where c + w1 > 0.565 and the coin is below 0.5; 'wobble only' and 'full-throttle command only' switch one departure from normal driving off; 'neither' is normal driving only

interface.how: inspect.signature(ThrusterChainEnv.__init__); one reset(seed=0) and one step through gymnasium.make; the gymnasium registry

meta.nothing_trains: no learner is imported or trained; every number is exact simulation of fixed controllers, linear algebra on the environment's own matrices, or the bank starts themselves
